Jordan Henderson is busily going around geeing up Chelsea’s players, in exactly the same fashion as he did when he played in this stadium for 12 years. Everton are reportedly exploring a move for Napoli midfielder Kevin De Bruyne during the January transfer window as David Moyes looks to strengthen his squad for the second half of the season.

The Belgian international has emerged as a surprise target for the Merseyside club, with his uncertain situation in Italy potentially opening the door to a return to the Premier League.

#1312. Official: D’Aversa replaces Aquilani at Sassuolo

Sassuolo have appointed Roberto D’Aversa as head coach following the dismissal of Alberto Aquilani.

According to an official club statement, the former Torino and Parma coach has signed a contract until 30 June 2027 and will take charge of his first training session this afternoon.

“U.S. Sassuolo Calcio announces that it has entrusted the technical leadership of the First Team to Roberto D’Aversa until 30 June 2027,” the statement read.

D’Aversa will be assisted by Salvatore Sullo, and he will be presented to the media at the Mapei Football Center on Thursday at 12:30 CET [11:30 GMT].

Aquilani was appointed in June for his first Serie A job, but he paid the price for a dismal run. Sassuolo have taken one point from their last seven games, conceding 29 goals so far this season, and Saturday’s 3-0 defeat at Roma left them 17th, only one point above the relegation zone.

D’Aversa knows all about relegation battles. He replaced Marco Baroni at Torino in February and turned their season around before leaving in the summer, when Ignazio Abate took over. He’s best known for taking Parma from Serie C to Serie A in consecutive seasons.

His first game in charge will be after the international break.

#1311. Parkinson’s: beyond the brain

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Parkinson’s research has focused mostly on the brain, and the processes that lead to the death of dopamine neurons, which eventually causes the varied symptoms of the neurodegenerative disease. But given that research has not uncovered a genetic component for most people, what triggers the disease has remained elusive. Some researchers have begun to investigate how environmental factors — including exposure to herbicides, pesticides and air pollution — could be an important factor in the increasing number of cases. Others, meanwhile, have found that the clumping of proteins that drives the disease might begin in the gut rather than in the brain.

This film investigates these avenues of research, and shares what it could mean in preventing and treating the disease.

#1310. Rio Ferdinand claps back at fans mocking him for celebrating Man United's late equaliser against Aston Villa which left them in the relegation zone

Published: 14:15 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:16 EST, 10 November 2026

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at football fans who criticised his reaction on social media to Manchester United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Former United defender Ferdinand drew criticism when he shared a photo of himself celebrating after the Red Devils' dramatic comeback on Sunday afternoon.

Michael Carrick's side had looked down and out at 4-2 in stoppage time, but late strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu meant they earned a point from the game.

They did, though, remain in the relegation zone – however Ferdinand shared two snaps to his X account following full-time.

The first showed the 48-year-old with his head in his hands, and the second saw him celebrating. He captioned the post: 'From this to THIS!!! Carrick time!!!!!!!!!! Birthday weekend just got (a) tad better in the last 6 minutes…'

Fans though flooded the replies with criticism, questioning why he was 'celebrating a draw' and calling him an 'embarrassment'. Ferdinand, though, has now taken the opportunity to respond.

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at fans who criticised his response to Manchester United's draw with Aston Villa

'Let me just address something,' Ferdinand began on Rio Ferdinand Presents. 'On socials I put a picture up and little comment underneath of me going like that (celebrates).

'That's not me celebrating a point against Aston Villa, by the way, it's me celebrating a moment in a football match. It's what football does to you. It can take over your body, take over your emotions in a moment. That moment isn't the big picture.

'So all of these people saying his standards have dropped and he's celebrating a draw... I'm not celebrating a draw against Villa, I'm celebrating the moment and the fact we actually came back and showed a bit of character.

'It's always about that moment that when you calm down and you go, look where we are in the league, that's terrible, looks how things unfolded in the game, that needs work. But, in the moment, as a football fan, you are allowed to get carried away with it.

'That's what football does. If you don't know that or don't understand it or feel it, you're not a football person, so get out.'

Ferdinand hasn't shied away from criticising his former team-mate Carrick amid United's poor run of form that has left them in 18th in the Premier League table.

United came back from behind to draw 4-4 with Villa having looked down and out in the game

His assessment of Sunday's showing was more tame, with the ex-centre back describing the effort as full of both character and chaos.

He added: 'It's like we need a punch on the nose, or two or three, to start playing. But then, the flip side of it, it's character and ability plays a part in that.

'In the end, we could have won it. But they are giving us fans grey hairs. It's crazy football.'

As thrilling as Man United's fight-back may have been to some fans, manager Carrick was still forced to answer difficult questions at full-time.

Sky Sports' Patrick Davison asked the former captain what he 'expected to happen over the next few weeks' - suggesting a question mark still lingering over his tenure despite comebacks against Roma and Villa.

Carrick's response was understandably thorny, with the manager underlining that he 'probably' would not be walking away from the role.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week.

#1308. Why Man Utd Hired Erik ten Hag Over Mauricio Pochettino in 2022

It seems rather likely that Michael Carrick will be sacked as Manchester United manager during the current international break. GIVEMESPORT understands that Mauricio Pochettino has emerged among the three leading contenders to take over, along with fellow candidates Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann.

The Argentine is currently head boss of the United States men's national team, and won't come cheap, having recently extended his contract. However, there is a release clause of around $10m (approximately £7m), which could simplify the deal.

This isn't the first time Pochettino has been linked with the Man Utd job. In 2022, he was once again among the strongest contenders, but missed out with Erik ten Hag picked instead.

Ten Hag's time at Old Trafford was ultimately ill-fated. Although things started off well enough, with the Dutchman winning the League Cup and finishing third in the Premier League, things took a notable dip in 2023/24.

The club finished eighth that term on 60 points – which was, at the time, their lowest position in the top flight since 1989/90. A surprise FA Cup final victory over Manchester City kept him in the job heading into his third season, but he lasted until just October before being sacked in 2024, with the Red Devils languishing in 14th place with 11 points from nine Premier League games.

Fast forward to 2026, and Carrick is on the verge of being sacked, with Man Utd on just eight points after 10 league games, sitting in the relegation zone. Once again, Pochettino is linked with the English giants, but why didn't the club make their move back in 2022?

Mauricio Pochettino is a leading contender to take over as Man Utd manager, and he already has his own Dele Alli at Old Trafford.

As per reports at the time, Man Utd had three notable concerns about Pochettino, which made Ten Hag a more appealing candidate. Firstly, it was noted that the Red Devils feared Real Madrid would make a swoop for the then-Paris Saint-Germain boss at the last minute. They evidently felt safer with a clear run at Ten Hag, who was with Ajax.

Secondly, there was a simple matter of finances. It was more costly to try and prise the Argentine away from PSG than the Dutchman away from the Eredivisie side. Finally, the Old Trafford hierarchy were 'extremely impressed' in their meeting with Ten Hag, who set out clearly the steps to improve the club.

That third reason is quite interesting as Pochettino also met with the Red Devils during the manager search, but evidently didn't nail his job interview as well as Ten Hag. Despite that, according to The Athletic, the Argentine was said to be 'confident' of getting an offer, having already been courted for a number of years at that stage.

With that in mind, reports claim the coach was left 'shocked' when finding out that Man Utd had opted to hire his Dutch counterpart instead. It is also worth noting that the Man Utd squad preferred the appointment of Pochettino back in 2022.

Four years on, it looks as though the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and any other senior stars still on the books could finally get their wish.

#1307. Crystal Palace will sack Pierre Sage after disastrous 16-game spell - this is how his reign fell apart over late, intense sessions, dinner at the training ground and an unpopular assistant manager

Published: 10:17 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 10 November 2026

Crystal Palace players and club chiefs have grown frustrated over Pierre Sage's training methods, Daily Mail Sport can reveal - and the 47-year-old will be sacked having won just two of his first ten Premier League matches.

A 3-1 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday saw Palace drop to bottom of the Premier League for the first time in nine years and proved to be the final straw for club bosses, who will tell the Frenchman his time is up.

Daily Mail Sport understands that while the Palace players got on well with Sage, they were frustrated by his late training sessions – with some not starting until 4pm. The regimented routine required players to stay at the training ground for dinner on the night before matches, with some not returning home until 8pm ahead of a 2pm kick-off the following day.

The club's hierarchy, meanwhile, expressed concerns early in the Frenchman's tenure that he was not doing enough defensive work on the training pitch.

Sage's philosophy was that the best way to defend was having the ball, meaning training sessions focused on running, pressing and possession rather than defensive structure.

But the lack of focus led to a poor defensive record, with Palace conceding 30 goals in 16 matches across all competitions. Defending set-pieces and counter-attacks has been a persistent problem for Sage’s side.

Pierre Sage will become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season after a dismal spell at Crystal Palace

Palace sit rock bottom of the Premier League after winning just two of their first 10 games

Daily Mail Sport understands many players voiced fears they were being pushed too hard in training, with sessions the day before a game particularly intense. There were also significant concerns about the quality of Sage's backroom staff, with his assistant Jamal Alioui proving especially unpopular among the players.

While Palace's on-pitch struggles have been evident, the situation is precarious off the pitch, too. A significant number of staff have resigned amid dissatisfaction with the regime imposed by chief executive Sharon Lacey, with morale understood to be low. Sources have suggested that while Lacey is talented, she struggles to motivate her workforce.

There has also been considerable turnover among senior executives, with six departures over the past 18 months. Chief financial officer Mitesh Velani is set to add to that number in the coming months. One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that the disruption to the club’s business operations has the hallmarks of a club heading for relegation.

As Palace look to bail themselves out of trouble, Daily Mail Sport understands former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank is in pole position to replace Sage, with six-pointers against Hull City and Coventry City following the international break. Sean Dyche also has admirers at Selhurst Park.

Palace chairman Steve Parish first contemplated sacking Sage over his lack of defensive nous in September, but gave him a stay of execution after Palace kept a clean sheet in a spirited performance away at Leeds on the eve of the international break. However, that display proved an anomaly as Palace shipped 19 goals in the following nine games.

Palace have won just once in their last eight matches in all competitions, beating Fulham 1-0 in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

In September, Daily Mail Sport revealed tensions had emerged between Sage and Parish when the latter took a dim view of the decision to drop teenage defender Jaydee Canvot in their defeat by Ipswich Town.

Palace paid French club RC Lens £4million in compensation to appoint Sage in June after he won the French Cup, finished second in Ligue 1 behind Paris Saint-Germain and was named manager of the season last term. It was the first time in 10 years that Palace had paid compensation to appoint a manager.

Palace chairman Steve Parish (right) first contemplated dismissing Sage in September over a lack of defensive nous

Palace players found Sage’s training sessions too intense and struggled to adapt to the late schedule

Succeeding Oliver Glasner, Palace's greatest manager, proved too big a task for the 47-year-old.

Following Palace's loss to Liverpool, Sage insisted the Eagles have been playing better than their league position suggests and pleaded for more time.

#1305. Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot

David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

The lack of discipline in their ranks was exposed when Dan Burn scored a late consolation and ended up in a melee with James Tarkowski and Joelinton. But the issues Jaissle, who lamented that “we must improve”, has to correct are for another day: this contest belonged to Everton.

Thierno Barry had provided the finish that secured a trip to Fleetwood in December and what an opportunity it is for Moyes to make Everton semi-finalists in this competition for the first time since 2016. Whether Grealish will have a part to play in it remains to be seen.

Thierno Barry with Everton's third! 🔵 https://t.co/dyb8fKud8N

The last thing Everton needed on a night of such importance was a distraction. Grealish will have a tough job mending relations, particularly with Moyes, but there was a paradox: though he had caused a major issue for 90 minutes he became an irrelevance.

Moyes is impatient to give Evertonians a big day out and his only focus was on crossing this hurdle – for all that Newcastle have had a turbulent start to the campaign, they are dangerous opponents and you wondered in the fraught opening 30 minutes if they might exacerbate the hosts’ woes.

As Jaissle hopped and squirmed on the sidelines, imploring Newcastle forward, chances came and went: Harvey Barnes had a header saved, Fabian Schar tested Jordan Pickford from 30 yards while Vitalii Mykolenko and James Tarkowski made huge goal-saving challenges.

“We should have scored more goals,” Jaissle, who was dressed as if auditioning for the role of The Milk Tray Man, growled. “It [losing] was shocking as the game was not that bad.”

Moyes was infuriated by Everton’s initial inertia, so much so there was a point when the Scot prevented Merlin Röhl, his own full-back, from taking a throw-in until Tarkowski and Jake O’Brien had complied with his gesturing to get 10 yards further forward.

It might have looked old-fashioned but it worked. Suddenly Everton started asking questions, Hayden Hackney almost got on the end of a cross from Mykolenko, and it encouraged the supporters on the vertiginous South Stand to raise their voices and become more involved.

What they needed was a goal to set things alight and in the 34th minute, it arrived. Tyrique George won possession by Newcastle’s corner flag, the ball dropped at Hackney’s feet and he instinctively ushered it on to James Garner, who whipped a right-footed drive beyond Lukáš Horníček.

James Garner puts Everton in front against Newcastle in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 https://t.co/TzponbWyGU

The roar that greeted it was a mix of elation and wonder, relief and desperation. The locals have grown weary of seeing nights with potential end in disappointment but here was the foothold they craved and the opportunity they were ready to seize. Soon the lead would be doubled.

Hackney would score the goal, converting a super Barry cross, but let us acknowledge the fabulous refereeing of Farai Hallam, who waved play on when he might have whistled for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. And how Everton took advantage.

Hayden Hackney doubles Everton's advantage! 🔵 https://t.co/VIY0Iln3nI

It must be said the officiating this week has, in the main, been outstanding. Watching a match without the persistent spectre of VAR has been liberating and you can see the referees have felt free to make decisions on instinct.

The whole experience of knowing a contest cannot be re-refereed has been better for all. It will not catch on, sadly, because too many people have gone too far down the road with VAR, but we should embrace the purity of “old school football” while we can.

Evertonians – the Prime Minister included – certainly embraced the buffer of a second goal and the fact Hackney scored it also felt like a throwback: a player who was plucked out of the Championship in the summer and encouraged by Moyes to show he could make the next step up.

He did that and so, too, did Everton, their progress was assured in the 69th minute when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall dashed down the left and crossed for Barry to finish. Moyes puffed out his cheeks as it hit the net. He, more than most, deserved to enjoy this one.

#1304. Romano: Man Utd Open Talks With Pochettino's Agents to Replace Carrick

Manchester United have already made contact with their top manager target as they begin the hunt for Michael Carrick's replacement, according to a brand-new update from Fabrizio Romano.

Man United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada have decided to recommend to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that the club sacks Carrick during the international break, following a disastrous season.

Not only do United lie in the relegation spots in the Premier League having won only one of their 10 matches this term, but they have also lost two of their four Champions League fixtures, and been knocked out of the EFL Cup by Brighton and Hove Albion despite leading 2-0 against the Seagulls at Old Trafford after 10 minutes.

The Red Devils are a shadow of the team who soared to a third-place finish in the Premier League last term under the leadership of Carrick, and Berrada and Wilcox have decided it's time for a change.

United's players shouldn't get away without any criticism however, given the majority have been nowhere near the levels they reached in the 2025-26 campaign. Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes haven't helped the situation either by speaking out publicly against Wilcox and Carrick in recent weeks.

Even though Carrick remains in the job for now, talk has already started about how is going tor replace the 45-year-old in the dugout.

As GIVEMESPORT revealed on Monday evening, USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino is emerging as a leading contender for the job, while Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have also had their admirers on the United board.

Speaking on his latest video on Tuesday evening, Romano revealed that the Red Devils have already held talks with the representatives of Pochettino, who GMS understands has a $10m release clause in the new contract he signed in August.

Romano said: "They already had contact with Mauricio Pochettino, so he's a serious candidate for sure.

"Then, obviously, before appointing him, meetings, talks, discussions are still needed. But they know him; they know him well. Pochettino ticks several boxes at Manchester United in terms of international experience and much more. So he's a manager highly rated by Manchester. United, so he's in the running for sure.

"He's also open to getting the job. So Mauricio Pochettino would be open to taking this opportunity. Then we have to see if Man United decide to go all in and appoint Pochettino. So that's the question mark right now.

But Pochettino is in the running for sure. There have been discussions with his representatives.

Pochettino has emerged from nowhere really in the United manager race, given the main names mentioned in recent weeks when Carrick's job was in danger were Howe, Nagelsmann, Conte, Unai Emery and Fabian Hurzeler.

Prising either of the latter two away from Aston Villa and Brighton and Hove Albion looks to be an impossible job, with Emery close to signing a new contract at Villa Park and Hurzeler not willing to leave the Seagulls right now.

Pochettino has been a target for United before, but they opted to appoint Erik ten Hag on the occasion where he was very high on their shortlist.

Also speaking on Tuesday afternoon, the Athletic's David Ornstein hinted that the appointment of Pochettino is now the most likely direction of travel, with the club currently not pursuing Howe, Nagelsmann or Conte, despite links.

Of course, United still need to agree the approximate £7.5m fee required to prise Pochettino away from the USA job, although the timing isn't great from the nation's point of view, given they have a competitive match against Haiti to play on Saturday night.

The positive for the Red Devils is that the Argentine, who was described as 'world-class' when the US appointed him, is clearly open to taking the reins at Old Trafford.

Now we wait and see if club chiefs pull the trigger, and if we see the 54-year-old in the dugout to face Liverpool a week on Sunday.

#1303. Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

#1302. Man Utd Manager Target Simone Inzaghi 'Decides to Leave' Al-Hilal

It is looking increasingly likely that Manchester United will be looking to appoint their next manager in the coming hours or days, and one of their targets has just decided to leave his club, according to an Italian journalist.

Man United chiefs gave Michael Carrick a stay of execution following the successive defeats to Como and Bournemouth, although it is clear that they wanted to see an improvement in the next three matches prior to the international break.

Carrick lost the first of those as the Red Devils were beaten 2-0 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, and it looked as though it would be curtains for the 45-year-old when his team found themselves 2-0 down at home against AS Roma in the Champions League.

United produced a stunning comeback to win that 3-2, before Carrick found himself in a similar situation against Unai Emery's Aston Villa on Sunday.

His side were 2-0 down after just four minutes, but they twice proved their battling qualities to come from two goals down to draw 4-4, with their final two goals both coming in injury time.

It doesn't appear it was enough to convince Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada that he should continue in the job after the international break though, with the duo expected to recommend to Sir Jim Ratcliffe in meetings in Monaco this week that he should be relieved of his duties.

Should that happen, then United will be looking for their next manager, and there are plenty of names appreciated by the hierarchy.

GIVEMESPORT sources revealed that Mauricio Pochettino is emerging as a leading contender for the job out of nowhere, although the Red Devils will need to pay $10m to activate the release clause in his contract as the United States manager.

GMS understands that three free-agent managers in Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte also have their admirers on the board, as well as Simone Inzaghi.

According to a journalist in Italy, posting on X, the former Inter Milan boss has now decided to leave Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal when his contract expires at the end of the 2026-27 season.

While the fact that he may not be available until the end of the season could count against him, there is no doubt that INEOS will be on red alert if he has decided to leave his current role in 2027.

Inzaghi will be one of the best free-agent managers available on the market should he leave Al-Hilal, and not just because of what he has achieved in Saudi Arabia.

The 52-year-old has won 52 of his 69 matches in charge of Al-Hilal, having enjoyed similarly fruitful spells in his home country leading Inter Milan and Lazio.

Inzaghi may be from a background of the notoriously defensive Serie A, but we have seen the striker's attacking instincts come through in his teams' playing style instead.

When he left Inter, they had a goals-per-game record that sat just under two, with a goal difference of +237.

Not only did he win one Serie A title during his time in charge at the San Siro, but he also came close to winning the Champions League on two occasions, with the club beaten finalists in 2023 and 2025.

#1300. What Man United, with their seemingly addictive habit, must do now once Michael Carrick is sacked: IAN LADYMAN on Sir Jim Ratcliffe's trail of bad judgment and waste

Published: 02:00 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 07:53 EST, 10 November 2026

Those who were there will never forget the utter chaos of Michael Carrick’s last act at Old Trafford. But as the outgoing United manager clung on to his dignity like a life raft in those mad closing moments against Aston Villa, the current poster boy for United’s desperate demise sat on the bench in his tracksuit.

Diogo Dalot is an honest and by all accounts fully committed Portuguese full-back who has been a United player for more than eight years.

The 27-year-old was bought for his teenage potential by his compatriot Jose Mourinho in 2018 but has never trained on. He has never been good enough for a really top English club yet has made more than 250 appearances for the most famous one of all and has played for five different permanent managers.

On Sunday he was booed off by his own supporters when substituted after an hour. His had been a particularly grim performance but the boos were not about him, not really.

No they were not about Dalot but instead about the fundamental truth of what he represents. Namely a steady, grisly and unforgivable drain of footballing standards at United that actually began in the final days of Sir Alex Ferguson and has subsequently never stopped.

It is this that has taken United from Ferguson’s final valedictory title of 2013 to where they are today, the bottom three of the Premier League. It is this that has drained United of all their clout and reputation. It is this that has cost yet another United manager – a seventh – his job.

Diogo Dalot has become the poster boy for the decline under Michael Carrick as Man United seemingly plumb new depths

The outgoing club legend is not a good enough manager for United and his appointment was yet another mis-step by the club's hierarchy

Carrick is not a good enough manager for United. His appointment was an emotional mistake, one of many made by Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the band of misfits and hopefuls who are currently in charge of football operations.

With a better manager – a better coach – in charge of the current team, United would be in the top half of the league. The fact they sit 18th and resemble a Sunday League team that never gets going until they have shaken their hangovers off is squarely down to him.

Nevertheless, United are a football club that exists to win trophies, no matter what the majority owners the Glazers may have said recently. But United will not win the big trophies again until they buy better players and by that I mean better footballers and better people.

It sounds simple, trite even. But it’s a simple truth of our game. Until United can reverse a seemingly addictive habit of paying too much money for too little, the difference made by a manager will only ever be a matter of six or seven places in the Premier League standings. And United needs a much greater improvement than that until this vicious cycle of self-harm comes to an end.

There is so much wrong at the modern Manchester United away from the field. Much of it begins and ends with the hideous hubris and self-regard of Ratcliffe, a man so shot through with misplaced self-confidence that he still insists on being tailed everywhere by a journalist he has hired to write a book on United’s journey back to the top of the mountain. Suffice to say that one won’t be ready for this Christmas.

But the thread that links the final days of Ferguson and his chief executive David Gill through the years of Ed Woodward, Richard Arnold and John Murtough to these dark days of Ratcliffe’s INEOS control is simple. It’s sub-standard players.

Despite the financial drain of the Glazers’ stranglehold, United have spent in the region of £1.75bn on their first team in the last ten years.

It takes quite something to do that and take a club backwards. It takes quite something to do that and buy only one player – captain Bruno Fernandes – who can claim to have been consistently effective over his time at the club.

Somehow, though, United have managed it and it is this hideous trail of bad judgment and waste that follows the current team and those that have come before it every time it runs out on to the field.

United are weak off the pitch and even weaker on it. Their football mirrors their off-field strategy. Haphazard, wasteful and inconsistent.

A number of years ago – at a time when previous CEOs Woodward and Arnold were trying to mend a broken club - they enlisted the advice of Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton and former captain Bryan Robson to help them work out what exactly a United team should be.

‘Exciting, daring, confident and humble’ were the key words they laid down. Well, what on earth happened to any of that?

United have a huge decision to make – yet again – over a new manager. The field of suitable candidates is not as big as they would like. Nor is United as attractive a proposition as it was. The demands are enormous yet the foundations shake. It’s not a good combination.

A good coach would improve them. Carrick has had two central defenders on his staff in Jonny Evans and Jonathan Woodgate. What on earth have they been doing for the last two or three months?

Long before the arrival of Jim Ratcliffe former chief executive Ed Woodward and Richard Arnold attempted to draw a blueprint for the club

Their successors in the boardroom Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have not impressed over a baffling summer

But United remain four or five good transfer windows away from where they need to be and the last time they put a run of good business like that together at Old Trafford Carrick was probably in the first team.

United need proper talent but they also need proper people, not the kind who would rather moan to TV cameras after a defeat than go home and think about their own part in what has just happened.

Last summer’s strategy seemed to have come straight out of Chat GPT and reflects terribly on the current football director Jason Wilcox. To ‘fix’ the midfield through three signings with the need to ‘fix’ the back four kicked down the road for 12 months is not so much a strategy as an exercise in transfer suicide.

Some think Wilcox should follow Carrick through the door on the back of that and it’s a reasonable point of view. Viewed through the mist of an autumn afternoon on Sunday, Wilcox looked as grey as his recent track record. An alternative take is that the recruitment of players like Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha is indicative of an uptick in returns, at least in part.

Whichever path you wish to walk, it simply has to lead to an improvement in the one area that will either nourish or starve a football club. With that in mind, the first question a prospective manager should ask is who is buying the players and on the back of what long-term strategy.

Carrick’s United team have looked like exactly what they are this season, a group put together by different people following different principles for different managers. How strange that it hasn’t worked.

United, as we know, needed a left-back over the summer. Lewis Hall, of England and Newcastle, may have been an option. Instead, United placed their faith in Luke Shaw, a 31-year-old with a long history of injuries.

Shaw, unsurprisingly, is currently injured which brings us back to where we started, namely the sight of the right-footed Dalot labouring out of position on the left of Carrick’s back four against Villa on Sunday.

You could say we saw this coming. Many did. In the dressing room and in the stands at Old Trafford. Carrick? He knew about it, too, but then he was only the manager.

His exit will hurt for a while. He is an emotionally intelligent and empathetic individual who will reel from the trauma of the last ten weeks. Over time he will realise that he is well out if it, though. When he took the job last summer, Ferguson is known to have been concerned about what it may do to him. As often, Carrick’s old boss was right.

United are set up to fail and Carrick’s replacement will realise that soon enough. When he walks into the first team dressing room for the first time and looks for those upon whom he can rely to consistently help him, too many eyes will be focussed on the floor.

#1299. Sir Alex Ferguson Had No Doubt Man Utd Legend Was 'the Greatest British Player of All Time'

From English icons Wayne Rooney and Paul Scholes to global stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Eric Cantona, former Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson worked with some of the greatest footballers of all time throughout his hugely successful 27-year spell at Old Trafford.

Widely considered one of the greatest managers in history, Ferguson built his reputation on winning. He remains the most successful manager in Premier League history, having secured 13 league titles and an incredible 38 major honours during his Manchester United tenure.

The two worked together relentlessly at Old Trafford and the former striker's talent was timeless according to the legendary Scot.

Despite managing an abundance of elite talent, Ferguson once singled out a former Manchester United attacker as ‘the greatest British player of all time’. Although he never got the chance to work with him personally, the player's exceptional skill, creativity and influence ensured his place in the club's history.

Ferguson, according to the Mirror, once labelled former Manchester United star George Best ‘the greatest British player of all time’, describing him as a truly ‘fantastic’ footballer:

"He was such a fantastic footballer. I think everyone at Manchester United looks upon George as one of the best players of all time. And I think that's the way we should remember him.

"In football terms, within this club, and the history of English football, then I would have to say that there has been no better British player."

Ferguson continued: "When you talk in world terms, the problem with Bestie is that he never played in a World Cup Final or World Cup semi-final.

“Players in that situation are denied the chance of being assessed among the greatest players in the world. Nonetheless, George is up there in the pantheon of great players.”

Best is often recognised as one of football's most gifted natural talents. He arrived at Manchester United as a teenager in 1958 and became a key figure in the club's success throughout the 1960s.

Found an error? Send it info@www.givemesport.com so it can be corrected.

The Northern Irishman played 470 times for the Red Devils, registering 179 goals and 61 assists. During his time at Old Trafford, he helped the club secure two First Division championships and the European Cup in 1968.

That same year, he also claimed the Ballon d’Or, becoming the only player from Northern Ireland to have won the prestigious individual award.

After spending the opening 11 years of his senior career at Old Trafford, Best left Manchester United in 1974. He subsequently embarked on a remarkable journey, representing around 14 clubs in countries including England, Scotland, Ireland, Australia, South Africa, China and the United States.

Best was renowned for his incredible ability on the pitch, with his mesmerising dribbling, technical quality and knack for deciding matches setting him apart from his contemporaries. His footballing brilliance earned admiration from some of the sport's biggest names, including Brazilian legend Pele, who once selected Best as one of his favourite footballers ever.

#1298. Real Madrid star Endrick opens up amid Milan and Roma links: ‘I don’t know what will happen’

Endrick admits he doesn’t know what will happen in January, but he has made it clear he wants regular football as Milan and Roma monitor his situation at Real Madrid.

According to Calciomercato.com, the 20-year-old Brazilian looks set to leave the Bernabéu this winter. Real Madrid would prefer a loan, like his spell at Lyon last season, but both Serie A clubs want better terms: either a permanent deal or an option to buy with a high buy-back clause for Real.

Endrick is under contract until 2030 and earns a reported €6m gross per season. Real paid Palmeiras €35m plus €25m in bonuses for him in December 2022, and he’s now valued at about €60m.

“I’m still young, I’m only 20, I don’t have to take off and throw myself off a cliff,” he told Globo. “Let’s see what happens. I can only say that I want to play, be happy, help my teammates, score goals and provide assists, like I did at Lyon. That was one of the best things that’s ever happened to me and one of the happiest times of my life.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, it’s all in God’s hands. I’m only asking to be able to do what’s best for my career. Whatever happens, happens.”

Endrick has played only a few minutes with Kylian Mbappé ahead of him, although he did feature against Roma in the Champions League.

“You all know who we have at Real Madrid and who’s ahead of me. Mbappé is a great player, he came second in the Ballon d’Or. I try to take the opportunities I’m given and do my best.”

He also praised José Mourinho, who said before the Roma game that the forward wasn’t going anywhere.

“Mourinho is a great person. Every day he comes to me and asks how I am, but he never talks about football. He wants to know about my private life. I like his attitude, he cares. I’ll always give my all for Real Madrid, which comes first.”

#1297. Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick

So where do Manchester United go from here? It is never a good look when opposition fans start willing a rival club to stick with their manager, but that was the ignominy that had befallen Michael Carrick by the end of an afternoon in which Lisandro Martinez’s latest plastic hardman impression embodied the very worst of United’s self-sabotage.

After seeing their team go 2-0 up when Cole Palmer converted the penalty given away by Martinez’s lunacy, the Chelsea fans taunted Carrick with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and later “You’re going down with the City”, a nod to the other Manchester club who are crisis torn for very different reasons.

As the final whistle loomed, though, and with United just grateful Estevao had not punished Martinez’s red card more severely, the Chelsea fans had changed their tune. “Michael Carrick, we want you to stay,” came the chant from the Matthew Harding Stand and that cut far deeper.

And to think that the opening 45 minutes had offered United and their fans some hope of a little respite from the storm before ultimately giving way to an ever-darkening gloom.

Carrick, who had been given a stay of execution in midweek, said he still expected to be in charge for Roma’s visit to Old Trafford on Tuesday in the Champions League. But it is hard to escape the feeling that another managerial change will be coming at United before too long even if no one can be sure what happens next.

Equally, the prospect of more upheaval in the dugout might elicit little more than a shrug from fans pointing the finger squarely at the ownership and the executives they have appointed. The players were spared this time but Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers remained the target of sustained abuse as did Jason Wilcox, the director of football.

Defeat here extended United’s winless run to nine matches, their worst sequence for 38 years. They have taken just four points from the last 21 on offer in the Premier League and seem to be sinking fast. Carrick was asked about the team becoming mired in a relegation battle. This is the territory United are in.

The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

By the end, with Estevao – making the most of a first league start of the season – running riot and Chelsea smelling blood, Carrick would have been relieved the scoreline was not worse. But he will also have wondered how United could again have found themselves in such a position after an enterprising first half when they attacked with pace and purpose and looked a very different team to the one that had been ransacked by Como and Bournemouth.

Michael Carrick said he expects to be in charge of Manchester United next week despite Lisandro Martinez’s moment of madness leaving the club mired in a relegation battle and on their worst run for 38 years.

United were urged to sell Martinez after the controversial Argentina defender was sent off for elbowing Wesley Fofana as Carrick accused his side of “unravelling” as they slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

It left United without a win in nine matches, their worst run since 1988, and at risk of being sucked into the relegation zone. They have won just two of 13 games this season.

The Old Trafford hierarchy gave Carrick a stay of execution in midweek and, when asked if he expected to still to be at the helm when United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, the head coach replied: “Yes. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”

Having been booked moments earlier for a foul on Morgan Rogers, Martinez was sent off for a second yellow. The incident came less than three weeks after the Argentinian was fined and publicly apologised for attacking United director of football Jason Wilcox and the board over transfer policy and was the latest in a series of mistakes from him on the pitch this season.

Joe Cole, the former Chelsea and England forward, believes United must get rid of Martinez.

“Whatever the next Manchester United looks like, Lisandro Martinez has run his course,’ Cole said on TNT Sports. “He’s at the scene of the crime too often for Manchester United and is at fault for moments and goals like that. So that’s probably his time done.”

Carrick refused to publicly criticise Martinez but admitted his dismissal was a “huge moment” and felt his team “unravelled” in the second period.

“Things have gone against us in a big way,” the United manager said. “It’s unravelled quickly. There’s a lot of emotion right now. It’s a huge moment in the game. Sometimes you get setbacks in games and you’ve got to deal with that better. I’ve not seen it [the Martinez incident] back so I don’t know if it was [a red card] or not. He’s gone to it and the referee gave that decision, but it’s a big moment.”

Asked if there would be a stigma attached to United potentially dropping into the relegation zone, Carrick added: “Not for me, no.”

And when asked how his players would deal with a relegation battle, Carrick added: “We’ve got to keep moving forward and winning games. There’s no words I’m going to explain to you now that makes any difference, it’s not going to change it. We’ve got to move forward and win matches.”

What do football fans actually want from their club owners? The model for most has been Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan and friends at Manchester City, owners whose hands are put frequently into pockets of unlimited depth, have made vast improvements to every aspect of the club and its community and are rarely ever seen, let alone heard from.

That view may have to evolve after certain verdicts about certain charges, but few envious glances from around the country have been cast towards the owners of Manchester’s other major club.

Manchester United’s accounts for last season suggest that ownership could be changing in the next three years, with a route to Sir Jim Ratcliffe assuming full control by 2029. But who would actually be the better custodians for United?

We know it’s not been good enough. It’s obvious to say that. But it’s something we can flip and we are the ones who can control that. That’s the beauty of it for me. We are in control of it and know there’s something we can do about it.

I don’t need any assurances [from the board]. I totally understand what’s needed here. I’m just focused on winning games.

If there’s anything I take about beyond these four walls it’s how the supporters are thinking. That’s all that matters to me. I’m not interested [in external noise in the media etc], my only focus is on making us better.

[Do you think the players are behind you?] One hundred per cent, for sure.

Thirty years ago when Newcastle United were coming off the bridle in the title race with Manchester United, Alex Ferguson, as he then was, accused a Leeds team, who had been in freefall since the new year, of professional malpractice when they put in a rare display of passionate commitment and tenacity at Old Trafford in a 1-0 defeat.

“Why are they not in the top six?” asked Ferguson. “To me they’re cheating their manager. #1296. Premier League ‘Dodgy’ Stick Users Can Expect ‘Knock and Talk’ Visits

If you read that and made anything between an audible gulp and a vintage Gary Neville, 'Oooo', the chances are you're well aware of the 'dodgy box/Fire Stick' trend that has arisen among Premier League fans in recent years - and for anyone who has one, it could soon mean a knock at the door as part of an impending crackdown.

That's according to ex-police detective turned television presenter, Rav Wilding, who recently appeared on the BBC's Morning Live programme to warn that the criminal Amazon Fire TV Stick market and similar 'jailbreak' streaming loopholes are set to be combated by new detection methods and more stringent investigations.

So, woe betide those somehow managing to watch the 3pm kick-offs...

While plenty are familiar with the TV license people sending initial emails, even cautionary texts, strongly worded emails and letters, before eventually turning up at homes and trying to quiz people on their devices and service use, not everyone is aware that these increasingly popular workarounds are currently being used by millions and, if anything, have only become more rife of late.

Of course, many are quick to turn away these kinds of inspectors regardless of whether or not they're flouting the licensing rules, but as per Wilding's recent insight, while "owning a stick itself is not a crime", using them to illegally access content certainly is.

Full list of UK and Ireland areas targeted in 'dodgy' Fire Stick crackdown have been named

Given the rising costs of broadband packages and, notably, broadcasting deals when it comes to the likes of the Premier League and other top-flight football competitions, specifically, these sticks have offered an alternative way to watch live sport, pirated versions of movies that have only just been released, series that have already aired overseas, and more via illegal apps.

Essentially, an estimated four million people in the UK alone are believed to be in possession of these sticks, and police are already clamping down on distributors and other parties harder than ever, which will inevitably mean looking into those paying these people for these premium, albeit counterfeit, subscription services.

As he goes on to explain, once authorities have the details of these sellers, "they’re going through their accounts" and, you guessed it, "seeing who has been paying money for these illegal things", adding that "people should possibly expect a conversation or two" when officers ask why they've been carrying out these transactions.

In fact, Kieron Sharp, the chairman of the Federation of Copyright Theft (FACT), is said in a statement issued to the Daily Mail:

“We have a wide range of enforcement options — from issuing cease and desist notices to 'knock and talk' visits — through to full criminal prosecutions where appropriate."

"We will take robust action against those involved, not only targeting sellers and distributors, but also those facilitating and profiting from the illegal activity.”

Once again, we know this won't be a problem for the vast majority of you, but for hypothetical individuals now checking to see their bank statements and history of transactions, or those who, at the very least, have been considering copping one of these dodgy boxes: we'd recommend you think twice and tread carefully.

#1293. Ballon d'Or 2027 Power Rankings

Harry Kane recently won the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but it's already time to look forward to what the next year of football will bring.

More importantly, who will be in contention for the prestigious individual prize in 12 months' time?

Much of that will hinge on which teams claim the biggest trophies, including league titles and the Champions League.

In the past, the prestigious individual accolade was based on the performance of players across a calendar year. However, the votes are now based on the results of the season.

Despite being a full year away from the 2027 ceremony, we've listed – and ranked – the players who are best placed to win the Ballon d'Or based on their respective teams' chances of success as well as their early-season form.

We've determined the order based on the following:

Desire Doue already looks like he's stepping up and becoming one of the most important players Luis Enrique has at PSG. With Bradley Barcola gone and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia absent for several months, the 21-year-old will be crucial.

He finished 14th in the 2025 Ballon d'Or and will be looking to improve on that next year. Having missed out on the 30 nominees in 2026, Doue has started the new season with eight goal contributions in 11 appearances for the French champions.

Will Ousmane Dembele regain the Ballon d'Or and join the exclusive club of players who have won the award more than once? If he can get back to the form that saw him crowned in 2025, there's every chance.

PSG are aiming for three Champions League titles in a row, and Dembele will now be vital to those plans with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia sidelined long-term. He's never been the most clinical in front of goal and only has four goals this season so far, but the France international brings pace, skill and technical ability to any team he plays for.

Is there a better all-action midfielder or set-piece maestro in world football right now? Except for his compatriot Jude Bellingham, the Arsenal and England star has no equal as things stand. Nobody is questioning that £100 million transfer fee now, following his big-money transfer from West Ham in 2023.

Rice inspired Arsenal to their first Premier League title since 2004 and was desperately hoping to follow that triumph with World Cup glory this summer. If he can repeat his form during the current season, he will reinforce his status as one of the world's best midfielders.

Erling Haaland is going to be under the microscope even more in the coming months. He'll need to block out the noise at Manchester City to continue his unbelievable form in front of goal.

The Norwegian became one of the most popular players in the world after taking the 2026 World Cup by storm. His big personality and inevitability make him a likeable footballer.

It's rare to see Man City or Norway play a game without Haaland finding the back of the net. That has continued into the 2026-27 season, as he's already on 14 goals for his club in all competitions.

England's first Ballon d'Or winner since Michael Owen in 2001, Harry Kane was crowned the world's best footballer in October 2026 after another magnificent year with Bayern Munich and England.

The England captain became his nation's top goalscorer in 2023, as well as reaching second place in the all-time Premier League scoring charts after scoring an incredible 213 times for Tottenham. His move to Bayern has been a roaring success to date, as he's managed to win back-to-back Bundesliga titles.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: In taking just 104 games to do so, Harry Kane became the fastest player this century to reach 100 goals for a club playing in one of Europe's top five leagues.

Kane looks set for another stellar campaign in 2026/27. He's already scored 10 times for Bayern Munich, with 10 assists as well, while he starred for England in the first international break of the season, hitting the back of the net six times in four matches, including braces against Croatia and the Czech Republic.

Jude Bellingham may have struggled to produce his best form for Real Madrid week in, week out last season, but the all-action midfielder re-announced himself on the biggest stage at the 2026 World Cup.

While that tournament won't be relevant for the 2027 Ballon d'Or, it proves Bellingham is capable of producing magic, while also possessing the 'clutch' gene. If Jose Mourinho can help him get back to his best consistently, the former Birmingham City youngster will be in contention for the biggest awards in 12 months' time.

He's started the 2026/27 campaign brilliantly. After an outstanding performance in England's 7-0 rout of Croatia in the Nations League, Roy Keane said that he could go on to become one of the greatest players ever.

Jude Bellingham for Real Madrid in 2026/27

Raphinha is one of the players who can feel most hard done by after being left out of the 2026 nominees altogether. The Brazilian has been brilliant for several years at Camp Nou, and has even transitioned into a new role seamlessly.

Having previously played on both flanks, the versatile forward has taken to the centre-forward role exceptionally well. Raphinha already has 15 La Liga goals to his name in 2026-27, and 19 in all competitions. His red-hot form makes him an early favourite for next year's award.

Michael Olise will certainly be in the mix if he keeps his breathtaking form up in 2027. The Frenchman broke the World Cup assists record in 2026, proving his worth as one of the best playmakers on the planet.

Having finished ninth in the voting for the 2026 award, Olise will be aiming for the podium at least next year. His cool demeanour allows the winger to remain composed in high-pressure situations. A skill many other Ballon d'Or winners have possessed.

Olise has started the 2026-27 season with a bang, earning Man of the Match as Bayern Munich beat Borussia Dortmund 2-1 in the German Super Cup. Weeks later, he earned another Man of the Match award after scoring two brilliant goals in Bayern's Champions League opener against Bodo/Glimt.

He also caught the eye with a hat-trick and two assists in a 7-0 league win over Union Berlin before scoring two superb goals in Zinedine Zidane's first two games as France boss.

Michael Olise for Bayern Munich in 2026/27

Kylian Mbappe has long been destined for the Ballon d'Or. The French forward has been touted as a future successor to Messi and Ronaldo, two of the greatest football players of all time – but now in his mid-20s, he's edging closer to cementing his status as the world's best footballer with an absurd amount of goals to his name season-on-season.

Mbappe, who scored 256 times for Paris Saint-Germain across 305 appearances, took a few months to get going at Real Madrid. But after finding the net 58 times for club and country in the 2025-26 season, there are few better finishers in world football. He already has double-figure goals in 2026–27.

Real Madrid have missed out on the biggest trophies in recent seasons, which has harmed Mbappe's chances at the biggest individual prize. If he can end his wait for Champions League glory, the sharp-shooting Frenchman will be at the front of the queue once again in 2027.

Despite narrowly missing out in 2026, Lamine Yamal could still become the youngest-ever winner of the award next year. His remarkable ability, combined with his superstardom, makes him something of a shoo-in in years to come.

Having already put one of the biggest clubs in Europe on his back since he was 15 and helped lead his country to a European Championship at 16, Yamal is clearly a fearless individual who embodies the phrase "if you're good enough, you're old enough."

After spending a season on loan at Barca, Marcus Rashford was blown away, calling Yamal his most talented teammate ever, before adding:

"If he ends up winning seven Ballon d'Ors, it wouldn't surprise me."

Barcelona's performance in the Champions League could play a big part in Yamal's fate. He's also started the 2026-27 campaign with Barcelona and Spain in scintillating form and is looking worthy of the Lionel Messi successor label. A

#1292. Oddo on the Italy national team: ‘Our talent needs more support’

Massimo Oddo believes the Italy national team still has the same problems as in recent years, and he has called for more support for the country’s young talent.

Speaking to TuttoMercatoWeb, the 2006 World Cup winner says the problems need to be fixed at the source, as Roberto Mancini prepares his side for Thursday’s Nations League game against France at San Siro.

“The national team now has the same problems as in recent years. They have to be solved at the source if we want it back at the very highest level,” Oddo said. “We need to work with the youngsters, who should have different goals from the ones they have today, and the same goes for coaches. The Italian game also needs more support.

“It takes courage, because the talent is there, as the Under-15s and Under-17s show, but it needs backing. Many kids get lost along the way for reasons that have nothing to do with the pitch, such as the regulations, the huge number of foreign players and too much impatience. What’s missing is the hard graft of working your way up. Compared with when I was young, kids now want everything straight away, even when they’re not ready. Without support, they waste time they need to develop.”

Oddo coached Milan Futuro, the Rossoneri’s Under-23 side, and he believes the system works. The problem, in his view, is that players reach it too late.

“If Sinner always played the world No 100, he wouldn’t learn anything more, but if he plays Alcaraz, he improves. The problem I saw personally is that the kids get there late, and 20 is late. Abroad, they’re playing first-team football at 17. Here they’re stuck in the Primavera, and those three lost years are years of talent held back.”

Mancini has also had to look further afield. He named teenagers Riccardo Cassano and Simone Lontani in his latest squad, and he’s trying to persuade Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi to choose Italy over Germany.

Oddo also praised his 2006 teammate Gennaro Gattuso, whose Lazio side are top of Serie A.

“I’d be a hypocrite if I said I expected it. I don’t think anyone expected to see Lazio like this. They’re doing amazing things. They have ideas, identity and spirit. I know Rino, and I know that when there are problems outside the dressing room, he pulls the group together and shuts everything else out.”

#1291. Mauricio Pochettino Appointment Can Save Lisandro Martinez's Man Utd Career

Manchester United are in a crisis, and the board look set to make the decision that a change is necessary.

United sit 18th in the Premier League with just one win in 10 Premier League games so far this season, while they have won just 3 of 14 in all competitions under Carrick, and GIVEMESPORT sources understand that the iconic former midfielder is set to be relieved of his duties at Old Trafford as a result.

Speculation has been rife for several weeks about his future, and who could potentially replace him, and it has now emerged that USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino is currently a leading candidate for the role.

The Argentine has got plenty of Premier League and Champions League experience, having managed Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, and Chelsea before taking up his role as boss of the United States, where he led the team to the Last 16 at the 2026 World Cup, before being rewarded with a new four-year deal.

But that contract is understood to have a $10m (£7.4m) release clause, which could open the door for him to return to England once again, and finally get the Man Utd job he has been pining for since 2019.

His arrival would be a mark of intent from INEOS, and potentially a final roll of the dice for board members like Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, who have so far failed to live up to their reputation of being 'best in class' since being brought in.

However, on the pitch, his appointment could also be a saving grace for some players or a dagger in the heart for others, who may not fit in with his style of play or how he sees football.

One player who could potentially be handed a reprieve at Old Trafford under the 54-year-old is his fellow countryman, Lisandro Martinez, who has been strongly linked with an exit away from the club in 2027.

The central defender has been in terrible form in recent weeks, having been at fault for a number of goals, before a ridiculous red card against Chelsea led to the team's collapse in a 3-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge. But more than that was his public outburst against the club hierarchy, where he admitted to feeling let down by the summer business and the strength of the squad. He has been labelled as being part of a 'toxic' culture at the club by pundit Adam Joseph.

Martinez is out of contract at Man Utd at the end of the season, and while the club have the option to extend by a further 12 months, reports have suggested they will not be looking to trigger that.

But with Pochettino being a manager who likes to dominate possession and build up from the back, the quality that Martinez has and his leadership qualities will likely be huge for the coach when it comes to implementing his style in the short-term.

Martinez had been a firm fan favourite until this season, and should he be able to string together a run of top performances and United start to turn the season around, he would likely be back in the good books quickly. That could force INEOS' hand when it comes to his contract situation, and could also convince the player that he is at the right club after all.

With funds understood to be limited, finding a replacement immediately for Martinez will be difficult. Pochettino won't want to be handicapped anymore if he is stepping in mid-season, and that could be the perfect remedy for a reprieve.

#1290. Cisse: ‘I like pressure, Balotelli my Italy role model’

Milan starlet Alphadjo Cisse says Mario Balotelli is ‘without a doubt’ his role model as an Italian player, reveals the Rossoneri teammate who has impressed him the most and explains why he likes to deal with pressure.

Cisse held a press conference at Coverciano today. He joined his ex-Catanzaro teammate Mattia Liberali, who has also received his first senior Azzurri call-up in the current break.

Cisse is currently Italy’s top club scorer, having netted eight times across all competitions for Milan.

“I have the desire to always prove myself, to stay hungry, and to show my qualities. It’s been an intense few months, and I hope to have many more like them,” he said during his press conference, attended by Football Italia, today.

“Liberali’s biggest strength is definitely his play: his through balls and final pass are among his best qualities. As for a defect, I’d say he can be a bit touchy at times,” he replied smiling, when asked about Liberali’s qualities and shortcomings.

Cisse spent several months on the sidelines last season while on loan at Catanzaro.

“The injury was a difficult moment, but rehabilitation brought a positive shift. I handled it well; I approached the injury in the right way, and by the time I arrived at Milanello, my confidence was high,” he said.

“I chose Catanzaro because I wanted playing time, and both the coach and the sporting director wanted me.

“I can play in every position. I don’t know if I can say which one I prefer, but I can play anywhere in attacking areas.

“Being here is wonderful and comes with great responsibility. We’ve only been here a few days, but the impact has been very positive. We’ll have the chance to get to know each other even better in the coming days,” he added.

When asked about the Milan teammate who has impressed him the most so far, he replied: “Luka [Modric] would be too obvious, so I’ll say Mario [Gila].”

Milan coach Ruben Amorim has shown his trust in Cisse, and the promising Italian attacker is enjoying his time at the club.

“My Milan teammates welcomed me very well. There’s a big difference between Serie B and Serie A, but my teammates’ welcome made it easy to settle in,” he said.

“I owe a lot to Aquilani, who gave me great confidence. I’m sorry things didn’t work out for him at Sassuolo, but I’d bet he’ll have a great career as a coach.

“Quality makes the difference. Many young players are emerging in Italy now, more than in the past,” he continued.

“At Milan, I think winning is always the priority, whether it’s the Scudetto or any other competition. That’s the norm. Neglecting one competition for another isn’t right. At Milan, you have to try to win everything.”

Cisse mentioned Alberto Aquilani as an influential coach in his career, but who has had the biggest impact on his professional career so far?

“I don’t think it’s fair to give one person more credit than others,” he replied.

“In the first few months last year, Aquilani had a huge influence on me, but I owe a lot to everyone. [U21]Coach Baldini leaves a lasting impression. He’s a great person. I like pressure; it motivates me to do better.”

Cisse recently scored his first goals at San Siro and will return to the Milanese stadium in just two days, where he could make his senior Azzurri debut.

“The coach will make the decision. Returning to San Siro with the national team would be even more special. I’m very ambitious, and playing for the national team is a source of pride,” he said.

“As I said before, I think I have broad shoulders. Many players on the national team have been here a long time and have also won the European Championship. I respect them, and we have to take things step by step. My first thought is to make my debut, and then we’ll think about everything else later.

“France needs no introduction. Italy must always aim to win; that should be the norm for the Italian national team.”

Lastly, Cisse named his undisputed role model as an Italy international.

“Without a doubt, I’d say Balotelli. He’s always been a role model for me on the national team,” he concluded.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1289. Mauricio Pochettino's 'kill' team talk - when USA were already 3-0 up - convinces Man United fans he's right to replace Michael Carrick

Published: 09:23 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 09:57 EST, 10 November 2026

Excitement is already building among Man United fans at the prospect of Mauricio Pochettino taking charge, if Michael Carrick is sacked.

Carrick is taking training at Carrington today and his future is set to be decided on Wednesday when chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

If United choose to axe Carrick as expected, with the club in the relegation zone, USA boss Pochettino is the bookies' favourite to take the reins at Old Trafford and footage of a passionate team-talk has convinced some supporters that he would be the right appointment.

A fly-on-the-wall documentary series called Behind The Crest offered insight into the 54-year-old Argentine's management style and recorded his half-time rallying cry, with the USA 3-0 up in a game against Jamaica during the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals in 2024.

Pochettino is seen building himself up into a frenzy, telling his players: 'Every single ball is the most important ball. We cannot play like we are winning 3-0.

'We need to go there and show the mentality. Take the next 45 minutes seriously. Take it like it is 0-0 and we need to win the game. That is the only way we're going to improve in our mentality.

🚨📹 WATCH: Mauricio Pochettino’s half-time team talk with his side already leading 3-0 after the first half!🗣️ “No, we don’t concede. We CANNOT concede. We need to go there and KILL and PLAY.”THAT MENTALITY! 👀🔥#MUFC pic.twitter.com/aXuiZn20i3

Mauricio Pochettino's passionate half-time speech to USA players (above) has convinced some Man United fans he would be the right man to take charge is Michael Carrick is sacked

'Be respectful with ourselves, first we need to respect ourselves. We cannot just go there and say to ourselves, "okay 3-0, no problem, they concede, we concede". We cannot concede! We have to go there and kill!

'If you are tired, we have players on the bench who can make a clear, clear impact and desperate to play. We have to press all together. When you're tired you can say, "coach, I can do no more".

'Enjoy being serious, we need to score the fourth, fifth, the sixth. That is the way we grow and respect the opponent.'

Despite the rousing speech, the USA went on to lose the second half but came out on top 4-2 in the match.

The footage has been widely shared on social media in conjunction with Pochettino's links to the Man United job and plenty of fans endorsed the idea of recruiting him, perhaps longing for a manager who can fire up the players in the mold of Sir Alex Ferguson's infamous hairdryer treatment.

One wrote: 'That intensity is what i want to see at United, 3-0 up at half and still no letting off.'

Another posted: 'He is right man for this moment!'. But others were more skeptical, with one capturing the sentiment of other naysayers, writing: 'Even if you hype him he is still gonna fail... if the same board keep of making decisions.'

Pochettino's work with the USA national side earned more plaudits at the World Cup on home soil, where they played excellent football before being dumped out by Belgium in the last-16.

And another of Pochettino's half-time speeches was viewed as a crucial turning point for his tenure in the USA.

With the team drawing 1-1 against Australia in 2025, Pochettino ranted: 'That is football! If we want to compete and we are 1-1 because we have the quality, we need to show more quality in the next 45 minutes. Play together. If you make a mistake, I don't care, but communicate and fight. They [Australia] come and they fight. When are we going to fix that? The team is dead. You need to talk!'

It was the first time Pochettino lost his rag and raised his voice at players since taking charge and midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said the message of the speech was: '"We're American. We don't take s***." Even though he's Argentinian, he has that mindset of, "Look, this is what we do. This is who we are. This is what America's about." Even from an outside perspective, he showed us Americans what we're about. He really drills that into us.'

The USA won the game 2-1 and the manager later reflected: 'This speech helped and was a great opportunity for the coach to explain to the players what to expect on the pitch. It was a tough conversation, but I think it was necessary.'

Perhaps that tough love is what Man United's dressing room now needs.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport late on Monday night, Carrick is nearing the sack during this November international break after presiding over a horrendous start to the campaign with the club in 18th and been given a stay of execution.

It’s understood that the Old Trafford hierarchy would want to inform Carrick of their decision face to face, so there may not be any confirmation from the club until Thursday.

Pochettino, pictured managing Southampton against Sir Alex Ferguson's Man United in 2014, could bring the intensity fans have missed since their legendary manager departed

The 45-year-old turned up for work at Carrington at 7.15am on Tuesday to oversee training with the players who are not away on international duty amid increasing uncertainty over his future.

United sources maintain that a final decision has yet to be made, with the club reluctant to engage in a running commentary over Carrick's position.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino has a £7million release clause in his USA contract. However, it is yet to be determined the true value of prising Pochettino out as that figure doesn't include buying out his backroom staff.

It is also believed within Pochettino's deal that there is another clause which would allow him to leave his US role for particular high-profile jobs, such as at Old Trafford.

As of Tuesday morning, Betfair have him at 4/7 with out of work trio Eddie Howe (5/2), Julian Nagelsmann (5/1) and Didier Deschamps (15/2) the next favourites.
